title: Settlement, Delivery & Time Rules

sections.heading: Ex-Dividend Date (under T+1)
items: Ex-date = SAME business day as record date (regular-way)
Buy ON or AFTER ex-date → DO NOT receive dividend

sections.heading: Cooling-Off Period
items: MINIMUM 20 calendar days between registration filing & effective date
Deficiency letter PAUSES the clock; resumes where it left off (does NOT restart)
Allowed: tombstone ads, red herrings, indications of interest, due diligence, blue-sky filings
Prohibited: sales, sales literature, advertising (other than tombstone), accepting money

sections.heading: Regulation T (Payment)
items: Customer payment due: S+1 (1 business day after settlement)
Under T+1 settlement → effectively T+2 for customer payment
Extensions: request from FINRA/SRO; non-payment → 90-day frozen account

sections.heading: GTC Order Cancellation (NYSE)
items: Auto-cancel: LAST business day of APRIL & OCTOBER
Day orders expire end of trading day

items.Deadline: 30 days; copy to RR same window
File electronically on EDGAR at time of sale order

sections.heading: Timeline Anchor (Quick Recall)
items: T = trade | T+1 = settle | S+1 = pay (Reg T)
20 cal days cooling off → Effective Date
Apr/Oct last biz day → GTC purge

common_traps: T+2 is OUTDATED — all equities, corps, munis, options & Treasuries now settle T+1 (eff. 5/28/2024). Ex-date = record date, NOT one day before.
Reg T payment is S+1 (1 day AFTER settlement), so effectively T+2 from trade date — students confuse it with T+2 settlement.
Deficiency letter does NOT restart the 20-day cooling-off clock — it pauses and resumes.
APO of NMS securities has NO prospectus delivery requirement post-effective date (0 days) — easy to forget; most often confused with the 25-day IPO rule.
GTC orders auto-cancel only in April & October (not quarterly, not monthly) on the LAST business day.
